layers.note: A small herb of meadows, open woods and grassy slopes.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −25 to 10 °C; gone below −35 °C and above 14 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −42 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −50 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 8 to 24 °C; gone below 5 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 800 to 6,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 400.

degree_days_5.note: About 200 to 4,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 80.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.35, gone by 0.2.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Early blue violet grows across much of North America from Alaska to New Mexico (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
